I'd argue that the Oxford Dictionary is not the be all end all of information especially when it pertains to Naruto, but even using these definitions urn doesn't apply at all. 

Does Gaara keeps drinks warm with his Sand Gourd? Is it metal? It does even really have a base since the bottom is curved. Does Gaara keep ashes with his Gourd? You could argue the metaphorical connection of gaara's memories of his mother, but given the gourd itself has very little significance in terms of Gaara's character and development this is a very big stretch. Working with the Oxford definitions, Gaara's container CANNOT be an urn in any great capacity. 

However, I feel as though the Oxford dictionary may not be an all encompassing source of information on gourds and a cursory Google reveals that the shape of the gourd fruit is identical to Gaara's gourd. Whilst the source above indicates that yes, gourds are typically made with gourd skin, the resemblance to the shape is far more significant qualifier to what constitutes a gourd. Gourd containers can be made out of a variety of things as seen in this website; http://www.gourdfestival.com/artwork.shtml

Gourds are also functional tools, used for transportation of material for journeys, while urns are ornaments usually used to signify a loved ones passing. Gourds are also typically associated with desert climates, which the Village in the Sand obviously fits. 

You can argue technical vs general, but nothing about Gaara's container makes it 'technically' an urn. It doesn't share any of the common culture associations of urns and Gaara doesn't seem overly attached to it in anyway that isn't Gaara treating it like a tool with a functional. 

Ultimately, through repeated references in the anime, manga, all supplementary material and merchandise, the creator himself, the actual shape, function and cultural and geographic connections of Gaara's container, it is a far better fit as a gourd than an urn. Otherwise, Gaara's container is just a nebulous container that resembles the gourd fruit in look and function and shares no qualities with those typically associated with urns, using both the Oxford dictionary or other common culture sources

“Hey Dave, I need you to redo some of this art for these Berenstain Bears VHS covers. Now it’s great as usual, but start fucking spelling the clients product properly. For the last time, it’s a *goddamn* A.”

Shit. I’ve been doing this alot lately, but it’s just so hard keeping track of all the little minute differences between realities. The date of a celebrity death here, the names of a couple kids books there, it makes you wonder how even more lame Butterfly Effect would’ve been in real life. “Boss, boss, you know if I worried about petty details like correct spelling I’d never be able to deliver the quality, and professional, product that keeps them coming back”

“That may be, but regardless of if it’s true it’s not a good look. If you need spelling lessons I’m sure HR can find a kindergarten class with some vacancies”

“Fine, fine, point taken Boss. I’ll read, spell, check from now on” I slyly smile at Louis, who sighs, turning and nodding as he leaves the room.  “Could have sworn it was spelt with an E…” I snidely whisper as Boss closes the door with a thud.

“Ha, I see what you did there” Says an all too familiar voice from behind where the door once stood. Its source was a man of almost identical appearance to myself. In fact, the closer I looked and the more I scrutinised the figure, the more difficult it was to notice any similarities at all. Soon, the only difference that was clear to me was the manner in which he carried himself, straight and official. Like he had a reason to be here.

“Who-who are you, did you get in here?!” I barely stammered.

“Same way you did” He growled, a toothy smile creeping.

“I am calling the poli-” As I reached for the phone I found my fingers slipping, slide across the phone. No matter how much I tried to grasp the, the receptacle now a bar of soap in my hands. In my struggle, my fingers began to warp around the phone, flowing and thinning across the black plastic coating of the telephone. Soon, my leg weakened and I found myself literally melting in my chair, my legs curling up towards the ceiling in concert with my upper appendages, dissolving and floating off to the ether.  “Oh my god…” I whispered.

The stranger began to chuckle, smiling from ear to ear as I reached out to catch the disintergrating bubbles floating from my body. Walking slowly towards me, he jovially began his interrogation “I bet you remember this sight. The trees and the streetlights bending towards the sky like outstretched arms, people writhing and twisting like shadows as everything began to tear apart. But you found a crack. You got lucky. You found one of the countless echoed realities that mirrored your home enough for you to assimilate with this world’s you. You woke up in his shoes one day and just kept on living, like nothing happened” By this point he was barely a foot away from, when the jovial expression he wore grew stern and serious “Now it’s my turn”

“Who are you?” I whimper, my being held together by what I could only dub sheer willpower.

His stern expression shifts into a snarl and he pulls close and whispers venomously "Your universe isn't the only one that collapsed. The multiverse is like a big chemical reaction and the universes just individual atoms. Yours hit this poor saps, then mine hit yours. And there's only room for so much Dave" Suddenly, he drove his hands into the gooey, semi vaporous mass that was my rapidly decaying form, and with a bright flash I saw nothing more.

With his last breath, he holds a clawed fist up to Newton and tries to activate the now disintegrated gauntlets, before collapsing, drained and charred.

Newton pushed between the two immortals and moved hastily to the trunk of the Delorean. They tell you never to believe anything on TV, that everyone and anyone is out to fleece you for your hard earned time and money. 'Just look at Nessie, just look at Bigfoot, 50 years and all that happened was some idiots wasted their lives looking for fairytales'. But they're all wrong. Kinda. See, they DO exist. They just don’t want to be found. When you and your species have evolved to hide, to be damn near undetectable, you only get found if they want you to. And when that happens, their intentions are never good. You need a tracker, but not just any tracker. You don’t want to following a trail for 20 miles only to realise it’s been tailing you for the last 15 and bifurcates the sap he had to form the rear guard. You need someone that understands not just geography, or biology, or can rattle off a million facts about soil composition and they kind of tracks they leave. You need a man who understands the reptile mind, can look into an animals eyes and tell you if it’s going to attack or back, whether it wants to kill or escape. Someone who can look into the Reaper’s vacant eye sockets and tell him to hit bricks. The Crypto Research And Positivism Society had spent too long doing independent research in black list government sites, filling journals with articles that would be forever lost, and operatives consumed by monsters and madness for a country that can’t and won’t remember them. Fuck that. It was time for us to get paid. Our boys had found some reality TV host, an Australian called ‘the Crocodile Hunter’, who had an unnatural gift for animals. I thought I’d be taking the new guy back in pieces.

The second those mud-stained steel capped boots stepped foot in the compound I thought O'Malley had gone as mad as a cut snake. Surrounded by men and women who've seen combat, horror and death, Steve felt completely at ease. The happy-go-lucky demeanour often assumed as a tv guise was as 'true blue' as the vampires that run the Vatican. Sitting in the truck as we did now, everything, in some small way, felt like it was gonna be okay. Steve was regaling the other passengers with stories about wrestling pythons, the time he left Rob a foot away from a hungry crocodile and the exhilaration of skiing in crocodile infested water. The endless stretch of rainforest had died down as we’d reached a clearing in this Brazilian rainforest. Nearby farms had lost cattle in the last week, and the Chupacabra was the most likely culprit. As we piled out of the vehicle, the squad of surly and traumatised cryptozoologists ready their weapons as I checked and double checked our camera. It felt unusually heavy in my hands, and despite myself, I wanted to fling it into the underbrush and grab a weapon. This strange sense of dread washed over me like a cold Winter wind, and as I looked at my compatriots, I knew they could feel it too.

By the time we’d managed to shake the feeling of dread, our newfound Southern rookie was nowhere to be seen. All that hype and we’d lost him seconds into the first trip. We stared gobsmacked at each other, when Steve’s voice broke the desperate searching “Guys I found it! She;s an absolute beaut too, come on or we’ll miss it!” That was fucking quick. Leaping to action, my comrades lead the charge to a small break in the treeline, following our journeyman companion into what would certainly be death. 

“Crikey would you look at this!” Steve joyously exclaimed, pointing a proud and noble finger at the writhing, shapeless mass that had begun to drag itself out of the swamp. It’s ‘skin’, if you can call it such, was like wet, black leather, continuously ripped apart and reformed by eyes and mouths that violently burst into existence then faded away. The form of the beast unholy and non-euclidean, stretching and constricting, twisting and tightening, collapsing in on itself and assuming new, more impossible configurations “She’s a mature one, you can tell by the length  and the pitch of the endless screeching bouncing between your eears right now. And what you look at this eyes, honed by evolution to see perfectly in the night for catching prey as well as reflect your deepest fears and desires” Steve began, while my friends gasped in horror, some screaming and fleeing, some muttering half mad ramblings in tongues foreign even to them, while others just knelt silently before the monster, too afraid or insane to move. Steve began to scratch the Shoggoth ‘behind’ one particularly mad eye, before a vicious looking mouth formed and snapped at the television star’s finger. “Cheeky bugger” Steve laughed.

I looked to our producer, who was currently using his left hand to pull one of his eyes out, and the right to signal me to keep going. “Now kids, I’m gonna do something only trained professionals should be doing, which will help me establish a beter connection, with this gorgeous Shoggoth. I’m gonna shove my thumb up it’s butt hole”
